summary: A scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies, Jackson studied at Columbia under Edward Delavan Perry and Edward Washburn Hopkins, and at Halle-Wittenberg. At Columbia, he was a fellow (1883–1886) and professor (1895–1935).

Proffitt specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a master's at the University of Colorado and a PhD at the University of Michigan under Micah L. Auerback, becoming an assistant professor at SUNY Albany around 2015.

Tagore worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and the Government College of Art & Craft, and held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1929).

Rehman worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Ahmad Hasan Dani and completed his PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later serving as assistant professor of archaeology at the University of Peshawar (attested 1988).

An Indologist and linguist, Bergaigne studied under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1877), the Sorbonne (from 1877), and the University of Paris (~1885–1888).

An Indologist who studied under Rambhadracharya, Mishra served as head of Sanskrit at Himachal Pradesh University, Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and visiting professor at the University of Indonesia.

MacBain is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at McMaster University (attested 2008), where she studied with Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, Mark MacWilliams, and Michael Greenwald.

An Indologist, linguist, and Iranianist, Anquetil-Duperron studied at the Sorbonne, Amersfoort, and under Darab Kumana. He served at the Bibliothèque nationale (1754), Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (1763, 1785), Académie Française, and Institut de France (~1795–1805).

Sachs was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist. After earning his degree at Johns Hopkins University (~1933–1939), he held posts at the Institute for Advanced Study (1945) and Brown University (~1948–1983).
Specializing in Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies, Yohannan studied at Columbia University (~1894–1898) and held a post there from ~1895 to 1925.
A scholar of Tibetology and religious studies, Zablocki earned his PhD at Cornell University and held an appointment at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).
Buddharakkhita studied under U Nārada and Mahasi Sayadaw, and taught Laurence Khantipalo Mills.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, Bayer earned his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, later serving as a research associate at the University of Munich (2004–2006).
Dash works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He was a Commonwealth Visiting Fellow at the University of Oxford (1997–1998) and held a post at Dr. Hari Singh Gour University (attested 1999).

An Indologist and linguist, Bezzenberger studied under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen and at Munich. He was a Privatdozent at Göttingen (1874) before serving as professor (1879), Prorektor (1890–1891), and Rektor (1919–1921) at Königsberg.
Kuhn was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp at the University of Berlin. He served as a teacher, professor, and director at the Köllnisches Gymnasium between 1837 and 1870.

Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at La Trobe University under Greg Bailey and later served as senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).

A scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, Hardy studied architecture at Cambridge. He held professorships at De Montfort University (~1993–2003) and Cardiff University (~2003–), and directed PRASADA.

Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, and studied under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers.
Schlombs is a scholar in sinology, history, and archaeology who served at the Museum of East-Asian Art (1991) and the Museum für Ostasiatische Kunst Köln (~1991–2022).
